text.p: Morgan Stanley Dean Witter said Friday it has maintained its outperform rating on Brazilian steelmaker Usiminas with a target price of $14.
-- "We consider the company to be the higher-quality Brazilian steel producer and an excellent play on growth in the Brazilian auto sector," Morgan Stanley analyst Hillary Peruzzi said in a report.
-- An outperformer, the stock has corrected 11.2 percent so far this month. "We consider the stock a very attractive value at current levels," Peruzzi wrote.
-- Based on estimates, Usiminas is trading at a discount to its global peers, the analyst said.

-- Usiminas' second-quarter net income of $75 million, or $0.335 per share was six percent below estimates but showed a "significant improvement" over $46 million in the same period last year, the analyst said.
-- The difference between result and forecast was due to higher-than-expected income taxes, Peruzzi said.
-- Projected slower Brazilian economic growth in the second half poses increased risks for Usiminas but "we believe that the fundamental positive story remains in tact," the analyst wrote.
-- Usiminas preferred fell 0.87 percent to 11.40 reais at 1230 local/1130 gmt in Sao Paulo while its common was untraded at its July 22 closing price of 10.72 reais.
